text:
maya: quick q — I'm getting a 401 when streaming from node using REDWOOD_API_KEY from .env. Works locally if I run curl with the literal key, but fails when using process.env. any obvious gotchas?

tj: are you sure there's no trailing newline? i had that bite me before — try xxd on it.

maya: hmm maybe. I used pbcopy on mac; could be a trailing \n. How do you usually check? :thinking_face: 

liam: pbpaste | xxd -> will show 0a at end if newline. Also double-check whether you're using Bearer vs Basic. our hosted endpoints expect Bearer tokens in Authorization, not Basic, unless you're doing a legacy client.

maya: ahhh i'm using a pre-existing client that builds a Basic header. header is: Authorization: Basic $(Buffer.from(`${apiKey}:`).toString('base64'))

tj: ok — Basic needs username:password. if you're using the API key as username with an empty password you must include the trailing colon BEFORE base64. if your env has a newline, Buffer will include it and the base64 will be wrong.

sarah: pro tip: printf '%s' "$REDWOOD_API_KEY" | base64 to avoid the newline. in node just use apiKey.trim() before encoding.

maya: will try trim(). weird part: it only fails when streaming (fetch + ReadableStream). non-streaming requests with the same client sometimes succeed. anyone seen streaming + auth header get dropped? node18 fetch had a redirect quirk that dropped Authorization on cross-host redirects.

liam: redirects can drop Authorization. check response.redirected or set fetch option redirect: 'manual'. but if you get 401 immediately it's likely key formatting.

maya: tried trim() and printf -n, still 401 only when running in docker (alpine). curl from host works. any docker-specific secret gotchas?

tj: alpine's /bin/sh builtin echo can be odd but the typical culprit is mounting a secret file that contains a newline. docker-compose env_file will read the file with the newline included. prefer passing env via environment: or using ARG/ENV without mounting the secret text file.

liam: quick checks to run inside the container: docker exec -it <svc> sh -c "printf '%s' \"$API_KEY\" | xxd" and also "printf '%s' \"$API_KEY\" | base64" — compare to host output.

maya: thanks. one more question — should we add a short troubleshooting note in the SDK docs about trimming and docker env files? i can make a tiny PR.

sarah: yes please. add a blurb under "Auth setup" with these points: use Authorization: Bearer <key>, always trim env values in examples, and a one-liner to check for trailing newline. include the node snippet.

sarah: ```js
const apiKey = process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY?.trim();
const res = await fetch(url, { headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${apiKey}` } });
```

liam: and one-liner for xxd: printf '%s' "$REDWOOD_API_KEY" | xxd

dev-bot: reminder: if you open a docs ticket, link it to DEVEX-123 and tag @devex for review. :white_check_mark:

maya: filing the ticket now — i'll include the docker checks and node snippet. thanks y'all :raised_hands:
